messages.subject: Plot problem.
parts:
This is a neat tool, thank you.

Here is a web app that was pretty easy to knock-off by following the tutorials:

https://github.com/bnaras/sglr-pkg/tree/master/sglr

It's a full package one can install as usual and run via:

 shiny::runApp(system.file('webapp', package='sglr'))

There are two tabs, one for the power characteristics and one for the boundary.  The boundary plot doesn't show up the first time.  Once you press submit, all is well.  Any ideas?

(PS.  For the math and the hiding, I just hand edited the html from a skeletal ui.R...)

-Naras

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Plot problem.
parts:
Nice!

One piece of advice: if you get rid of the "sglr" directory and move everything in there into the root of the repo, then it's easier for people to install as you can then use Hadley's devtools::install_github function.

The boundary plot doesn't show up because of a bug/limitation in Shiny. The client sends the width/height of each plot output, as normal Shiny inputs, so the server can auto-size itself if desired. When a plot is in an element that's hidden, the size is sent as 0/0. Normally, as soon as you change the visibility of the container element, the width/height is recalculated and resent to the server. In this case, you're using a submit button, so that's stopping *all* of the inputs from being sent until submit is clicked--including these width/height values.

One workaround you could use for now is to provide an explicit width/height in your call to reactivePlot, e.g. reactivePlot(function() {...}, width=600, height=400). Either that or get rid of the submit buttons.

One other thing to note. You are using JQuery to show/hide the outputs as the input tabs change. (Was that the only reason you used an index.html file instead of ui.R? Or are you just more comfortable in HTML?) That's OK, but there is also a declarative way to do this in Shiny that you should know about. It is currently broken in your case due to the same problem I described above, but you should know about it anyway:
  1. Give <ul class="nav nav-tabs"> an id attribute, e.g. inputTab
  2. Change <a href="#tab-4469-1" data-toggle="tab" id="powerCalcInp"> to <a href="#tab-4469-1" data-toggle="tab" data-value="powerCalcInp">
  3. Change <div id="powerCalcOut"> to <div id="powerCalcOut" data-display-if="input.inputTab == 'powerCalcInp'">
  4. Repeat for boundary <a> and <div>
Now that's the way it's supposed to work; input$inputTab is now either powerCalcInp or boundaryCalcInp, and you can use data-display-if to control the visibility of arbitrary HTML elements based on that value. But it looks to me like the presence of the submit button breaks it. Since inputTab acts like every other Shiny input, its effect is delayed until submit is clicked, which is not what we want in this case. So if/when we fix the Shiny bug described above then you could move to this model, but probably not before that.
